clues.q: In Exodus, God first called Moses from this, which was on fire but was not consumed.
In 1 Samuel, this young shepherd defeated the giant Goliath with a sling and a stone.
In Genesis, this favorite son of Jacob was sold by his jealous brothers and later rose to power in Egypt.
In the book of Daniel, Daniel spent a night here after praying to God, and was found unharmed in the morning.
In Genesis 11, people built a city with a tower reaching toward the heavens, and God confused their language at this place.
In the book of Jonah, God sent this to swallow the runaway prophet, who spent three days and three nights inside it.
In Genesis 3, this crafty creature tempted Eve in the garden.
In Genesis 8, this bird returned to Noah’s ark carrying a freshly plucked olive leaf.
In Numbers 22, which animal speaks to the prophet Balaam after he strikes it?
In 1 Kings 17, God sent these black birds to bring bread and meat to a prophet hiding by the brook Kerith.
This beloved hymn begins: “…how sweet the sound, that saved a wretch like me.”
“Silent Night” was first performed on Christmas Eve 1818 in Oberndorf, a village in what is now this country.
The famous “Hallelujah” chorus comes from this oratorio by George Frideric Handel.
Blind from infancy, this American hymn writer wrote “Blessed Assurance” and thousands of other hymns.
Isaac Watts based this Christmas favorite on Psalm 98, though it never mentions a manger.
This 1998 DreamWorks animated film tells the story of Moses, from the bulrushes to the Exodus.
Cecil B. DeMille’s 1956 epic in which Moses parts the Red Sea and receives the law on Mount Sinai.
In this 1992 comedy, Whoopi Goldberg hides out in a convent disguised as a nun named Mary Clarence and transforms the choir.
This 1959 epic, famous for its chariot race, won 11 Academy Awards including Best Picture.
Liam Neeson voices this great lion in the 2005 film “The Chronicles of Narnia: The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe.”
In Acts 2, the Holy Spirit came upon the disciples with tongues of fire during this Jewish festival.
This Roman emperor called the bishops together for the Council of Nicaea in 325.
Taken to Ireland as a captive in his youth, this 5th-century bishop later returned as a missionary and became its patron saint.
In Acts 9, the future apostle Paul was struck blind by a light from heaven on the road to this city.
This North African bishop of Hippo wrote “Confessions” and “The City of God.”
Beginning in the late 1940s, these ancient manuscripts were found in caves near Qumran.
clues.a: What are the Dead Sea Scrolls?

clues.q: This Albanian-born nun, famous for serving the poor of Calcutta, received the 1979 Nobel Peace Prize.
This North Carolina-born evangelist became nationally famous after his 1949 tent revival in Los Angeles.
Pope John XXIII opened this gathering of the world’s Catholic bishops in Rome in 1962.
clues.a: What is the Second Vatican Council (Vatican II)?

clues.q: In 1965, Pope Paul VI and Ecumenical Patriarch Athenagoras lifted the mutual excommunications issued in this year.
In the Gospels, this camel-hair-wearing prophet baptized Jesus in the Jordan River.
This fisherman disciple denied knowing Jesus three times before the rooster crowed.
In Luke 19, this short tax collector climbed a sycamore tree to see Jesus pass by.
In John 2, Jesus turned water into wine at a wedding in this Galilean village.
This Roman governor of Judea presided over the trial of Jesus and washed his hands before the crowd.
This is the very last book of the Bible, full of visions given to John on the island of Patmos.
This Old Testament book contains 150 songs and prayers, including “The Lord is my shepherd.”
This New Testament book follows the four Gospels and tells how the early church spread from Jerusalem.
The second book of the Bible, its name means “going out,” for Israel’s departure from Egypt.
Which of the four Gospels is the shortest?
“Swing Low, Sweet Chariot” and “Go Down, Moses” are famous examples of these African American religious folk songs.
Martin Luther’s best-known hymn declares that “A Mighty” one of these “Is Our God.”
This co-founder of Methodism, brother of John, wrote “Hark! The Herald Angels Sing” and thousands of other hymns.
Often called the “father of English hymnody,” he wrote “When I Survey the Wondrous Cross” and “O God, Our Help in Ages Past.”
George Bennard wrote this hymn that begins, “On a hill far away…”
Mel Gibson directed this 2004 film about the last twelve hours of Jesus’s life, with dialogue in Aramaic, Hebrew and Latin.
clues.a: What is “The Passion of the Christ”?

clues.q: This 2006 film follows Mary and Joseph on their journey from Nazareth to Bethlehem.
Kelsey Grammer plays pastor Chuck Smith in this 2023 film about a hippie-era revival in Southern California.
In this 1965 film, Julie Andrews plays Maria, a lively postulant at Nonnberg Abbey who becomes a governess.
This 1981 Best Picture winner features Eric Liddell, a Scottish runner who would not race on a Sunday.
This apostle traveled the Mediterranean on missionary journeys and wrote letters to the Romans and the Corinthians.
In Acts 13, this companion, whose name means “son of encouragement,” set out with Paul from Antioch on their first missionary journey.
In Acts 7, this deacon became the first Christian martyr.
Issued in 313, this agreement between Constantine and Licinius granted Christians freedom of worship in the Roman Empire.
clues.a: What is the Edict of Milan?

clues.q: This 4th-century scholar translated the Bible into Latin in the version known as the Vulgate.
In 1978, Polish cardinal Karol Wojtyła was elected pope and took this name.
clues.a: Who is Pope John Paul II?

clues.q: Like his father, Martin Luther King Jr. was ordained a minister in this Protestant tradition.
Its young members were nicknamed “Jesus freaks” in this late-1960s and 1970s revival among hippies on the U.S. West Coast.
In 1957, Billy Graham held a crusade lasting about four months at this famous New York City arena.
This fellowship of churches was founded at an assembly in Amsterdam in 1948.
clues.a: What is the World Council of Churches?

questions.q: First book of the Bible?
How many disciples did Jesus choose?
Town where Jesus was born?
First man created in Genesis?
Garden where Adam and Eve lived?
On which day did God rest after creation?
Who led the Israelites out of Egypt?
River where Jesus was baptized?
Disciple who betrayed Jesus for thirty pieces of silver?
Town where Jesus grew up?
Judge whose great strength was tied to his uncut hair?
Mother of Jesus?
How many Gospels are in the New Testament?
Adam and Eve’s son killed by his brother Cain?
Abraham’s wife, who laughed when told she would have a son?
Son of David known for his wisdom?
How many days and nights did it rain in Noah’s flood?
Finish the short verse in John 11: “Jesus ___”?
Peter and Andrew fished on the Sea of what?
Jesus taught these words, which begin “Our Father, who art in heaven”?
Main original language of the Old Testament?
Original language of the New Testament?
Son of Abraham taken up Mount Moriah?
Mountain where Moses received the law?

clues.q: Anointed by the prophet Samuel, this tall Benjaminite became the first king of Israel.
clues.hint: Young David played music to soothe him.

clues.q: In 2 Kings 2, this prophet was carried up to heaven in a whirlwind, as a chariot of fire appeared.
clues.hint: His cloak passed to his successor, Elisha.

clues.q: In chapter 6 of his book, this prophet saw seraphim in the temple crying “Holy, holy, holy.”
clues.hint: His book is the first of the major prophets.

clues.q: In the book of Daniel, this king of Babylon threw Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego into a fiery furnace.
clues.hint: He also dreamed of a statue with feet of iron and clay.

clues.q: In 1 Kings 21, this king of Israel, husband of Jezebel, coveted Naboth’s vineyard.
clues.hint: His name is a palindrome.

clues.q: In Luke 15, this younger son wastes his inheritance in a far country, then comes home to a father who runs to meet him.
clues.hint: His father throws a feast with a fattened calf.

clues.q: In Luke 10, this traveler stops to help a beaten man after a priest and a Levite pass by.
clues.hint: He came from a region north of Judea.

clues.q: In the parable of the lost sheep, how many sheep does the shepherd leave to search for the one?
clues.hint: He started with one hundred.

clues.q: Jesus compared the kingdom of heaven to this tiny seed that grows into a large plant where birds can perch.
clues.hint: It is also a yellow hot-dog topping.

clues.q: In Matthew 25, five foolish young women waiting for the bridegroom ran out of this for their lamps.
clues.hint: The wise ones brought extra in jars.

clues.q: This Christmas carol tells of a good duke of Bohemia who looked out “on the Feast of Stephen.”
clues.hint: He and his page bring food to a poor man.

clues.q: Often sung to the tune “Old Hundredth,” this short hymn of praise begins “Praise God, from whom all blessings flow.”
clues.hint: Its name comes from the Greek for “words of glory.”

clues.q: Missionary Stuart K. Hine wrote the English version of this hymn, which began as a Swedish poem by Carl Boberg.
clues.hint: “Then sings my soul, my Savior God, to Thee…”

clues.q: This German Baroque composer wrote the “St. Matthew Passion” and the “Mass in B minor.”
clues.hint: He served as a church musician in Leipzig.

clues.q: A former sailor who became an Anglican clergyman, he wrote the words of “Amazing Grace.”
clues.hint: He was a curate in the English village of Olney.

clues.q: Russell Crowe builds an enormous ark in this 2014 Darren Aronofsky film.
clues.hint: The title is the builder’s name.

clues.q: Norman Jewison directed this 1973 rock-opera film based on the Andrew Lloyd Webber and Tim Rice musical.
clues.hint: Its title song asks “Who are you? What have you sacrificed?”

clues.q: In “The Ten Commandments” (1956), Yul Brynner plays this pharaoh who refuses to let the Hebrews go.
clues.hint: Egyptian name meaning “born of Ra.”

clues.q: This Best Picture winner for 1966 dramatizes Sir Thomas More’s refusal to approve Henry VIII’s remarriage.
clues.a: What is “A Man for All Seasons”?
clues.hint: Paul Scofield won Best Actor for the lead role.

clues.q: Robert De Niro and Jeremy Irons play Jesuits in South America in this 1986 Palme d’Or winner.
clues.hint: Ennio Morricone wrote its famous oboe theme.

clues.q: In Acts 28, after a shipwreck, Paul spent three months on this Mediterranean island.
clues.hint: Its capital today is Valletta.

clues.q: According to Acts 11, the disciples were first called “Christians” in this city.
clues.hint: It was a great city of Roman Syria.

clues.q: In 380, this emperor’s Edict of Thessalonica made Nicene Christianity the official faith of the Roman Empire.
clues.hint: He was the last emperor to rule both East and West.

clues.q: The fourth ecumenical council met in 451 at this city across the Bosporus from Constantinople.
clues.hint: Its name begins like a mineral called chalcedony.

clues.q: In his Easter letter of 367, this bishop of Alexandria listed the 27 books now in the New Testament.
clues.hint: He had attended Nicaea as a young deacon.

clues.q: This Oxford author’s 1952 book “Mere Christianity” grew out of radio talks he gave on the BBC.
clues.hint: He also wrote the Narnia books.

clues.q: Vatican II opened the door to celebrating Mass in local languages instead of only this ancient one.
clues.hint: The language of ancient Rome.

clues.q: Known by three letters, this widely used English Bible translation was first published as a complete Bible in 1978.
clues.a: What is the New International Version (NIV)?
clues.hint: Its initials sit between NIRV and NKJV alphabetically.

clues.q: This South African Anglican bishop, later archbishop of Cape Town, won the 1984 Nobel Peace Prize.
clues.hint: He was affectionately known as “the Arch.”

clues.q: In 1974, an evangelical Congress on World Evangelization met in this Swiss city and issued a covenant named after it.
clues.hint: It sits on Lake Geneva and hosts the Olympic Museum.

clues.q: In Judges 4, this prophetess and judge led Israel and sent Barak into battle.
clues.hint: She held court under a palm tree.

clues.q: Which woman told Naomi, “Where you go I will go, and your people shall be my people”?
clues.hint: She was a Moabite who married Boaz.

clues.q: This Jewish queen of Persia risked her life to save her people, “for such a time as this.”
clues.hint: Her cousin Mordecai raised her.

clues.q: In John 20, she was the first to see the risen Jesus, at first mistaking him for the gardener.
clues.hint: Her name points to a town on the Sea of Galilee.

clues.q: In Acts 16, this seller of purple cloth from Thyatira was baptized by Paul in Philippi.
clues.hint: She opened her home to Paul and Silas.

clues.q: With five loaves and two fish, Jesus fed a crowd of about this many men, plus women and children.
clues.hint: Twelve baskets of leftovers were collected.

clues.q: In John 11, Jesus called this man out of his tomb after he had been dead four days.
clues.hint: His sisters were Mary and Martha.

clues.q: In Joshua 6, the walls of this city fell after the Israelites marched around it and blew trumpets.
clues.hint: They circled it seven times on the seventh day.

clues.q: In Exodus 16, God fed the Israelites in the wilderness with this bread from heaven.
clues.hint: Its name means “What is it?”

clues.q: In 2 Kings 5, this army commander from Aram was healed of leprosy after washing seven times in the Jordan.
clues.hint: The prophet Elisha told him what to do.

clues.q: Phillips Brooks wrote this carol after visiting the Holy Land; it says “in thy dark streets shineth the everlasting Light.”
clues.a: What is “O Little Town of Bethlehem”?
clues.hint: It addresses the birthplace of Jesus.

clues.q: In the spiritual “Go Down, Moses,” the singer tells old Pharaoh this.
clues.hint: Moses repeats this demand in Exodus.

clues.q: Based on Lamentations 3, this 1923 hymn by Thomas Chisholm sings that God’s “mercies… new every morning.”
clues.hint: Its title praises God’s loyalty.

clues.q: Handel’s “Messiah” had its first performance in 1742 in this capital city.
clues.hint: It is the capital of Ireland.

clues.q: The hymn “Joyful, Joyful, We Adore Thee” is sung to the “Ode to Joy” melody from this composer’s Ninth Symphony.
clues.hint: He grew deaf yet kept composing.

clues.q: This 2008 Narnia sequel is named for a young Telmarine prince who calls the Pevensie children back for help.
clues.hint: His name sounds like a large inland sea.

clues.q: This actor played both Moses in “The Ten Commandments” and Judah in “Ben-Hur.”
clues.hint: He won the Best Actor Oscar for the chariot epic.

clues.q: Sung by Whitney Houston and Mariah Carey, this song from “The Prince of Egypt” won the Oscar for Best Original Song.
clues.hint: “There can be miracles…”

clues.q: Max von Sydow plays Jesus in this 1965 George Stevens film whose title calls it the best tale ever.
clues.a: What is “The Greatest Story Ever Told”?
clues.hint: Its title is a superlative about a story.

clues.q: After the Olympics shown in “Chariots of Fire,” Eric Liddell went to serve as a missionary in this country, where he was born.
clues.hint: He had been born in Tianjin.

clues.q: According to Acts 2, about this many people were baptized on the day of Pentecost.
clues.hint: Three followed by three zeros.

clues.q: In Acts 17, Paul preached at the Areopagus in this city, mentioning an altar “to an unknown god.”
clues.hint: Home of the Parthenon.

clues.q: The book of Acts is addressed to Theophilus, just like this Gospel.
clues.hint: Its traditional author was called “the beloved physician.”

clues.q: Athanasius wrote a famous biography of this Egyptian hermit, often called the father of monasticism.
clues.a: Who is Anthony of Egypt (Antony the Great)?
clues.hint: He shares a name with Cleopatra’s Roman partner.

clues.q: Around 110, this bishop of Antioch wrote seven letters to churches while being taken under guard to Rome.
clues.hint: A Spanish saint of the 1500s later took the same name.

clues.q: Bill and Vonette Bright founded this ministry at UCLA in 1951; it is known today as Cru.
clues.a: What is Campus Crusade for Christ?
clues.hint: Its original four-word name was dropped in 2011.

clues.q: Elected in 1958, Cardinal Angelo Roncalli took this papal name and soon called the Second Vatican Council.
clues.hint: Remembered as “Good Pope John.”

clues.q: Martin Luther King Jr. was pastor of this Montgomery, Alabama, church during the 1955–56 bus boycott.
clues.a: What is Dexter Avenue Baptist Church?
clues.hint: It is named for the street it sits on.

clues.q: Pastor Chuck Smith’s church in Costa Mesa, California, welcomed thousands of young hippies in the late 1960s and became this movement of churches.
clues.hint: Its name recalls the hill where Jesus was crucified.

clues.q: In 1956, Billy Graham helped found this evangelical magazine.
clues.hint: Its title names the faith and the present day.

questions.q: Which apostle was a tax collector before following Jesus?
How many books are in the New Testament?
In which city did the first ecumenical council meet in 325?
Which disciple would not believe Jesus had risen until he saw the wounds?
In Genesis, what sign did God set in the clouds as a promise after the flood?
Which Gospel begins, “In the beginning was the Word”?
In which city was Jesus crucified?
Whose twelve sons gave their names to the tribes of Israel?
Which New Testament letter contains the chapter “Love is patient, love is kind”?
In Mark 6, people in his hometown call Jesus by what trade?

rounds.name: Final Round
rounds.q: This fisherman apostle brought his brother Simon Peter to Jesus, and he is the patron saint of Scotland.
rounds.hint: His X-shaped cross appears on Scotland’s flag.

rounds.name: Final Round
rounds.q: This carol is the English version of the Latin hymn “Adeste Fideles.”
rounds.a: What is “O Come, All Ye Faithful”?
